title: Local Bernstein theory, and lower bounds for Lebesgue constants
summary: Classical (or ``global'') Bernstein theory establishes sharp control on entire functions of exponential type that are bounded and real-valued on the real axis. We localize some of this theory to rectangular regions $\{ x+iy: x \in I, 0 \leq y \leq y_0 \}$, showing that Bernstein-type bounds with acceptable errors can continue to hold for functions holomorphic in such rectangles, bounded and real-valued on the lower edge of the rectangle, at most exponentially large on the upper edge, and at most double exponentially large on the vertical sides.
